Zeus Electric Motorsport

Motor dyno test jig

Designed, fabricated and tested · student EV team

The team's motor hadn't run in a long time. I designed and built the rig that held it on the dyno so we could prove it ran and performed under real, wheel-driven load.

  • Designed the jig from scratch in SolidWorks around the full load path: motor, sprocket, wheel, swingarm.
  • Fabricated the frame from welded hollow steel and added adjustable bearing-block arms that hold the swingarm at a set height.
  • Built a sealed sheet metal enclosure that guards the drivetrain and houses the electronics.
  • Designed a closed-loop liquid cooling system with custom-machined fittings, sized with hand calcs and checked in ANSYS.
  • Wrote the dyno test plan, logged power and temperature on a DAQ, and root-caused a chain and sprocket failure on the rig.

Zeus Electric Motorsport

Drive sprocket and mounting plate

Designed, analyzed and machined

The part that connected the chain to the wheel and completed the motor-to-wheel power path on the test rig.

  • Modeled the sprocket, splined hub and locking plate as one assembly, with fit and clearance checks.
  • Used FEA to find and strengthen weak spots at peak drive torque.
  • Set the fits with a tolerance stack-up and released a drawing with GD&T, finish and deburr notes.
  • Machined it in-house and iterated the backplate through several fit-ups until alignment was right.

Technische Universität Berlin · Research intern

Battery cell testing and thermal modeling

May – Aug 2026 · Fachgebiet Fahrzeugantriebe

Measured how lithium-ion cells wired in parallel share current and heat, using a test-to-model pipeline I built for 30 real cells.

  • Wrote the HPPC test plan and ran the cycler tests, then wrote MATLAB code that finds every pulse automatically.
  • Built a 6-stage MATLAB/Simulink pipeline: extract, estimate, validate, create, pack.
  • Modeled per-cell heat generation from first principles; the slow RC branch made most of the heat.
  • Caught a flawed first model and a sign error in the temperature model by checking outputs against physics.

University of Calgary · Research assistant

Robotic joint actuator test platform

Sep 2026 – present

A servo-driven joint with a harmonic-drive reducer, built as a test bed for current and vibration diagnostics.

  • Integrated a harmonic-drive reducer, Mitsubishi servo motor and custom mechanical parts, and designed the test fixture.
  • Wired a Panasonic FP-X0 PLC to an MR-JE-40A servo amplifier and ran the joint in position, speed and torque control.
  • Made stops fail-safe with normally closed contacts, so a broken wire stops the joint.
  • Collected vibration and current data with accelerometers and analyzed it in Python and MATLAB.
